clauses.clause: Explain concepts by interpreting texts.
Learn concepts by interpreting texts.
Construct texts to demonstrate understanding of concepts and processes.

verdicts.evidence:
Tell students that now they are going to write what they know about the major events and central message in Sun and Moon.
- Display the Sun and Moon response sheet.
- Distribute prepared clipboards and pencils.
- Focus students on Part III and read the prompt aloud, allowing adequate think time: 'Use words and pictures to show what happened in the story.'
- Direct students' attention to the box labeled Beginning.
- Invite students to whisper a response into their hands:
- Tell students that they may begin writing their response in the Beginning box.
- Repeat this process with the remaining two boxes, Middle and End.
- Circulate to support students as they write.
verdicts.rationale: Students interpret the story to explain and learn its concepts (major events, central message) and construct their own written and visual texts to demonstrate understanding.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Explain and learn concepts and processes by interpreting and constructing texts. (I/C)

clauses.clause: Identify the general purpose of a variety of texts.
clauses.note: Students discuss why the author wrote Sun and Moon (author’s purpose) for this text.

clauses.clause: Identify the target audience of a variety of texts.
clauses.note: No task asks students to identify or discuss the intended audience.

clauses.clause: Identify different modes of communication: print, digital, auditory, and visual.
clauses.note: While multiple modes are used (read-aloud, visuals), students are not directed to identify modes.

clauses.clause: Create texts in teacher-selected modes such as print, digital, auditory, and/or visual.
clauses.note: Students write and draw on a response sheet (print/visual mode) to show events and central message.

verdicts.evidence:
- Tell students they are now going to consider why the author may have written Sun and Moon.
- Direct students' attention to the Unit 1 Guiding Question anchor chart and complete the first column with the book title.
- Follow the same routine established in Lesson 9 to complete the three columns, culminating in a Think-Pair-Share for the third column:
- 'Why do you think the author wrote the book?' (Responses will vary, but may include: to imagine what the sun and moon might think about, and/or to describe the wonderful things that happen on earth at night.)
- If productive, cue students to expand the conversation by saying more:
- 'Can you say more about that?' (Responses will vary.)
- Cold call two or three students to share out their ideas.
- As students share out, capture their responses on the anchor chart.
verdicts.rationale: Students identify the author’s purpose for the text and create a written/drawn response, but they do not identify target audience or modes of communication.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Explain how authors of texts use language for a specific purpose and a target audience.

clauses.clause: Explore how context shapes the audience's responses when constructing texts.

clauses.clause: Interpret texts to analyze ideas.
clauses.note: Students interpret the story and analyze ideas by discussing why Moon changed its mind and identifying the central message.

clauses.clause: Construct texts to evaluate ideas.
clauses.note: Students construct brief written/drawn retells and note the central message, but they do not create texts to evaluate ideas.

verdicts.evidence:
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner:
- 'Why did Moon change its mind? What was the central message or lesson that Moon learned?' (Moon realized that the world is beautiful no matter if it's day or night, and Moon learned to appreciate his place in the night sky.)
- As students discuss, circulate and listen in. Take note of the ideas they are sharing and target a few students to share out with the whole group.
- Cold call a few selected students to share out.
verdicts.rationale: Students analyze the text’s ideas (central message and character change) through discussion, but the writing tasks focus on retelling and identifying message, not constructing texts to evaluate ideas.
verdicts.grounding_note: evidence quote found in lesson raw text
verdicts.standard_raw_text: Interpret and construct texts to aid the analysis and evaluation of texts and ideas. (I/C)
